concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
question: Which property of isobars is always different?
solution: The correct answer is __**Atomic number**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Isobars** are atoms of different chemical elements that have the same **mass number** (total number of protons and neutrons) but different **atomic numbers**. • The **atomic number** of an element represents the number of protons in its nucleus and is unique to each element. **Isobars always have different atomic numbers.** • The **mass number** (sum of protons and neutrons) is the same for isobars, which is why they are classified as isobars. • The **number of electrons** may vary between isobars since the atomic number (which determines the number of electrons in a neutral atom) is different. • Due to their differing atomic numbers, isobars belong to different elements and thus exhibit distinct **chemical properties**.
